## 2. RULING ON THE AttributeIdentity COMPARISON: **EXTRACT**

Probed live on Roslyn 4.14.0, a guarded type in `AgentGuard.CrossPlatform` applied as an attribute in an `AgentGuard.Engine` compilation. Identical results on the `AttributeSyntax` and on its rightmost leaf name node in **every** case:

| fixture | `GetSymbolInfo` (AttributeSyntax = name node) | `GetTypeInfo` (AttributeSyntax = name node) | compiler |
|---|---|---|---|
| well-formed, no-arg ctor | `Method: GuardedAttribute.GuardedAttribute()` | `Class: GuardedAttribute` | clean |
| well-formed, required arg supplied | `Method: GuardedAttribute.GuardedAttribute(string)` | `Class: GuardedAttribute` | clean |
| **malformed, required arg OMITTED** (the exact AG0008/AG0105 fixture shape) | **null, `OverloadResolutionFailure`, candidates=[ctor]** | **`Class: GuardedAttribute`** | CS7036 |
| malformed, qualified `[A.B.Guarded]` | null, `OverloadResolutionFailure` on the RIGHTMOST leaf; the two left leaves are `Namespace` symbols | `Class: GuardedAttribute` on the rightmost leaf; null on the namespace leaves | CS7036 |
| malformed generic `[Guarded<int>]` | null, `OverloadResolutionFailure` (on the `GenericName` node) | `Class: GuardedAttribute<int>` | CS7036 |
| unresolved identifier | null, reason `None`, no candidates | `Error: Guarded` | CS0246 ×2 |

**Ruling: extract.** Not reuse — the mechanics are `private` inside `AttributeIdentity` and its only entry, `IsAnyOf` (`:40`), returns a bool over a candidate identity set. Not duplicate — the two bodies would be the same logic with renamed variables (rails-dry-code rail 6). Tier 1 plus `ReferencedType` is literally `AttributeIdentity.cs:63-67`; tier 3 is literally `:69-71`.

**What this buys, and why the first round's design was wrong.** Round 1 proposed `GetSymbolInfo(...).Symbol`, skip when null — one tier. Measured, that **silently misses a guarded type applied as a malformed attribute**, the exact hole `AttributeIdentity` already closes for AG0008/AG0105. The contract calls that a defect: "a position the language allows and the rule misses is a defect, not a boundary."

**Why the extraction is safe for the general lens** — tier 3 is inert everywhere except the attribute case. Measured, every other way `GetSymbolInfo` returns null on a name node:

- overload-resolution failure on a plain method call (`G.M()` where `M(int)`): `M` leaf → `GetTypeInfo` **null**. Receiver `G` leaf still resolves to `NamedType: G`. (CS7036)
- inaccessible member (CS0122): `M` leaf → `GetTypeInfo` **null**.
- ambiguous type (CS0104): `Dup` leaf → `GetTypeInfo` `Error: N1.Dup` — rejected by the non-error guard.
- member group (`nameof(G.M)`): `GetTypeInfo` **null** — recovered by tier 2 instead, which is why tier 2 exists.
- unresolved identifier (CS0246): `GetTypeInfo` `Error: Guarded` — rejected.

So tier 3 adds the attribute recovery and nothing else.

**What stays with AG0008 and AG0105, in `AttributeIdentity`:** the syntactic fail-closed fallback (`MatchesSyntactically` `:77-90` and the `AttributeSyntaxName` normalization) and the candidate-identity question. It must NOT leak into the general lens: for AG0008 the fallback is fail-closed because the candidate set is a fixed known list, but for an assembly-scoped type rule a namespace-blind simple-name match reports unrelated same-named types — reporting wrongly, not failing closed. The unresolved case carries no namespace at all (`Error: Guarded`).

Existing tests that pin the extraction as behaviour-preserving, unchanged: `InteropOnlyInCrossPlatformLibrariesAnalyzerTests.MalformedSameNamedDllImportAttribute_WithRequiredArgOmitted_IsNotReported` (:165), `.UnresolvedInteropAttribute_IsReportedViaSyntacticFallback` (:203), `NativeCallbackBodyMustBeGuardedAnalyzerTests.MalformedUserDefinedUnmanagedCallersOnly_WithRequiredArgOmitted_IsNotReported` (:393), `.UserDefinedUnmanagedCallersOnlyInDifferentNamespace_IsNotReported` (:362). The new tier 2 never fires on an attribute (attributes give `OverloadResolutionFailure`, never `MemberGroup`), so none of the four moves.

**Where the extracted mechanics live:** inside `WrittenNameScanner.cs`, as `Resolve` and `ReferencedType`. It is the scanner's own core judgment, it adds zero files beyond the one the contract already reserved, and `AttributeIdentity` already depends on two shared helpers (`WellKnownType`, `AttributeSyntaxName`) so a third is the established shape. A fourth file holding two methods would be a new surface with no second responsibility.

## 4. ARCHITECTURE-TEST MECHANISM

One new class, `analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/AnalyzerLensOwnershipTests.cs`, building ONE `CSharpCompilation` over the analyzer project's own sources. Every step below was run and measured.

**Construction.** `RepositoryFiles.FindRepositoryRoot()` → `analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers`; enumerate `*.cs` recursively; skip build output through `RepositoryFiles.IsUnderIntermediateOutput` (both existing owners, reused). Parse each with `CSharpParseOptions(LanguageVersion.Latest)`, **plus one synthesized tree holding the seven `global using` directives `<ImplicitUsings>enable` generates** (Directory.Build.props:15) — the SDK's `GlobalUsings.g.cs` is not a repository file. References: every non-dynamic loaded assembly in the test process plus every `*.dll` beside `typeof(object).Assembly.Location`. Options: `OutputKind.DynamicallyLinkedLibrary`, `NullableContextOptions.Enable` (Directory.Build.props:14). Measured result: **82 files, 0 compiler errors**, every registration call and every kind argument resolved.

**How an ownership check tells duplicated scanning from unrelated analysis on the same kinds — three parts.**

**(a) Registration identity is resolved, never text-matched.** A node is a registration only when `GetSymbolInfo(invocation).Symbol is IMethodSymbol m` with `m.Name` starting `"Register"` and `m.ContainingType` under `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis`. A kind argument counts only when `GetSymbolInfo(argument).Symbol is IFieldSymbol f` with `f.ContainingType.Name` in `{SyntaxKind, OperationKind, SymbolKind}`. A local named `SyntaxKind`, a string `"IdentifierName"`, or a comment cannot satisfy either.

**(b) A kind set qualifies as a duplicate-scanning discriminator only when its members carry no meaning outside the lens.** Measured live:
- `{SyntaxKind.IdentifierName, GenericName}` — **0** registrations project-wide. Qualifies.
- `{OperationKind.VariableDeclarator}` — **1** registration project-wide, `ContractConcreteTypeMustNotBeReferencedAnalyzer.cs:52`, which the extraction moves. Qualifies.
- `{SymbolKind.Field, Property, Method}` — **13** registrations across 9 unrelated analyzers. **Does not qualify.**
- `MemberUseScanner`'s five operation kinds — 3 unrelated registrations. **Does not qualify.**

The test's own doc comment records these counts with file:line, so a later reader does not "improve" the check by adding a set that does not qualify.

**(c) For the sets that do not qualify, ownership is checked positively — by required CALL, resolved by symbol.**

**Check 0 — the compilation is clean.** `Assert.Empty(compilation.GetDiagnostics().Where(d => d.Severity == Error))`. Measured justification, not ceremony: with the global-usings tree omitted the same compilation produced 156 errors, and the same checks then reported **0** call sites of `MemberUseScanner.RegisterForAssembly` and **1** of `MemberUseScanner.Register`, where the truth is **2** and **17**. Without check 0 every "no duplicate found" answer is unfalsifiable. Same principle `AnalyzerRunner.ThrowOnUnexpectedCompilerErrors` (`AnalyzerRunner.cs:193`) already enforces for fixtures.
- positive fixture: an extra in-memory tree with a deliberate `CS0103` → the check goes red.
- negative fixture: the real 82 sources alone → green.

**Check 1 — written-name lens has one owner.** No file but `WrittenNameScanner.cs` passes `SyntaxKind.IdentifierName` or `GenericName` to a resolved `Register*Action`.
- positive: an in-memory `Planted.cs` whose `Initialize` calls `context.RegisterSyntaxNodeAction(Handle, SyntaxKind.IdentifierName)` → flagged.
- negative: a tree registering `SyntaxKind.InvocationExpression`, and a tree declaring `private const string Kind = "IdentifierName";` with a comment naming `SyntaxKind.GenericName` → not flagged, proving the check is symbol-resolved.

**Check 2 — carried-type lens has one owner.** No file but `DeclaredTypeScanner.cs` passes `OperationKind.VariableDeclarator`.
- positive: a planted tree registering `OperationKind.VariableDeclarator` → flagged.
- negative: a planted tree registering `OperationKind.Invocation` and `SymbolKind.Field` → not flagged, proving the 13 legitimate symbol-kind registrations stay green.

**Check 3 — every consumer calls its owner.** For each (file, required owner method) pair, at least one invocation resolves to that exact method symbol: `ContractConcreteTypeMustNotBeReferencedAnalyzer.cs` → `DeclaredTypeScanner.Register`; `EngineInternalsOneDoorAnalyzer.cs`, `OneDoorIntoCrossPlatformAnalyzer.cs`, `OneDoorIntoPerOsAnalyzer.cs` → `WrittenNameScanner.RegisterForAssembly` + `DeclaredTypeScanner.RegisterForAssembly` + `MemberUseScanner.RegisterForAssembly`; `EngineToBoundariesOneDoorAnalyzer.cs` → `MemberUseScanner.RegisterForAssembly`. This is the half that covers the two kind sets that do not qualify under (b).
- positive: a planted analyzer registering kinds inline instead of calling the owner → flagged as a missing required call.
- negative: a planted analyzer calling the owner → not flagged.

**Check 4 — the caller restriction is routed through `CompositionPoint`. This replaces the first round's absence-of-`"Create"`-literal check.** Two halves:
- (i) each of the four door-rule files contains an invocation resolving to the method-level `CompositionPoint` caller check;
- (ii) **every** read of `ContainingSymbol` on a `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis…AnalysisContext`, anywhere in the analyzer project, is an argument of an invocation whose resolved method's containing type is `CompositionPoint` or `OwnerClass`. Measured **green on landing: 7 reads, all 7 already flow that way** — `GuardedConstructionAnalyzer.cs:127/:137/:151`, `OwnerClass.cs:36`, `PresenceCheckOnlyFromApprovalGateAnalyzer.cs:82`, `TempRootBackDoorAnalyzer.cs:92`, `TimeMustUseTimeProviderAnalyzer.cs:71`.
- Strictly stronger than the literal check: you cannot hand-roll "am I inside `Create()`" without reading the containing symbol, and this catches it however the method name is spelled — a constant, a `nameof`, a shared string — all of which the literal check misses.
- positive: a planted tree with `if (context.ContainingSymbol is IMethodSymbol m && m.Name == FactoryName)` → flagged.
- negative: a planted tree with `CompositionPoint.Encloses(context.ContainingSymbol)` → not flagged.

**Check 5 — the type-reference extension stays off the Boundaries gate.** Within `OneDoorIntoCrossPlatformAnalyzer.cs` and `OneDoorIntoPerOsAnalyzer.cs`, every `WrittenNameScanner.RegisterForAssembly` and `DeclaredTypeScanner.RegisterForAssembly` passes `EngineAssembly.Name` (resolved as an `IFieldSymbol` on `AgentGuard.Analyzers.EngineAssembly`) and never `BoundaryAssembly.Name`; each file still holds exactly one `MemberUseScanner.RegisterForAssembly` passing `BoundaryAssembly.Name`. Structural counterpart to Acceptance 22, which is behavioural and can pass by coincidence.
- positive: a planted `WrittenNameScanner.RegisterForAssembly(context, BoundaryAssembly.Name, Inspect)` → flagged.
- negative: the same with `EngineAssembly.Name` → not flagged.

The compile-the-analyzer-sources helper is private to this one test class. It moves to `RepositoryFiles` (the existing owner of repository-source reading) when a second consumer appears — not before.

## 5. FULL TEST DESIGN

### Direct scanner tests

Two new files, each driving the scanner through a throwaway probe analyzer declared in the test file that reports one diagnostic per callback, run through `AnalyzerRunner.RunAsync`/`RunWithReferenceAsync` unchanged (Acceptance 18). Each asserts the exact set of (span text, resolved symbol) pairs — never `Assert.Single` where two nodes can fire.

`WrittenNameScannerTests.cs` — required reference forms, all probe-verified: `typeof(G)`; `nameof(G)`; `nameof(G.M)` (the `G` leaf → NamedType, the `M` leaf → Method **through the member-group tier**); cast; `as`; `is` pattern; `case` label; generic argument `List<G>`; **the generic name itself `GG<int>`** (its identifier is a token, so the `GenericName` node is the only node that catches it); generic constraint; base list and interface list; using-alias target and using-alias use (the alias use resolves straight through to `G`); `global::`-qualified receiver; field, property, method-return, parameter and local declaration positions; `var` local (measured: `var` is an `IdentifierName` resolving to the inferred type — the documented overlap with the carried-type lens); `new G()`; member names `G.M()`, `G.F`, `G.P` and the method group `Func<int> f = G.M;`; **well-formed attribute** (name leaf → the constructor; `ReferencedType` maps it to the attribute type); **malformed attribute, required constructor argument omitted**, declaring `"CS7036"` — the test that goes red if anyone reduces `Resolve` to one tier; malformed qualified attribute; malformed generic attribute.

`DeclaredTypeScannerTests.cs` — field, property, method return, each parameter, local, inferred `var` local, `List<G>` field, `G[]` field, pointer target under `unsafe`; a property's implicit backing field handed back once not twice; accessor and event method kinds skipped; the handed-back declaration's `Locations[0]` is the reported span (pinning AG0006's `ReportFirst`); `RegisterForAssembly` gating.

| input | W sees | M sees |

The first four are the fail-closed payoff: `MemberUseScanner` fails OPEN on every call that does not bind, so a bypass written as a deliberately-unbindable call slips past AG0023/AG0029 today. The written-name lens still catches the guarded TYPE. Policy for the fifth row: a name that resolves to nothing is NOT reported — the compilation already carries CS0246/CS0103 and the build fails on the compiler error, and `AnalyzerRunner` requires every fixture to declare its compiler errors, which Acceptance 18 forbids adding.

FORMS NOT COVERED, AND WHY EACH IS CORRECT:
1. A name in a `//`, `/* */` comment or inside a `<c>` doc tag — not a syntax node, binds to nothing, invisible to the compiler too. This is the sanctioned way to name a guarded type in prose, and it is the fix for D2.
2. A name inside a `#if`-disabled region — not in the active tree; the compiler does not bind it either.
3. Generated code — `ConfigureGeneratedCodeAnalysis(GeneratedCodeAnalysisFlags.None)`, matching every existing analyzer in the project. Consistency, not a hole.
4. A type reached by reflection string (`Type.GetType("AgentGuard.Engine.SystemServices")`) — no name node, no symbol, invisible to any analyzer design. Also outside AG0041's threat model: reflection does not need the `InternalsVisibleTo` grant the rule fences.
5. A `dynamic`-dispatched member — nothing binds; the compiler cannot check it either.
6. The `AgentGuard.Tests` compilation — deliberately not gated (contract), and the test proves nothing is reported there.
7. A pointer element as a COMPILED FIXTURE. The lens covers it (measured: `GuardedStruct*` → `IdentifierName` with `PointerType` parent; `TypeTree.cs:42` already walks `IPointerTypeSymbol`). But `AnalyzerRunner.cs:56` builds `new CSharpCompilationOptions(OutputKind.DynamicallyLinkedLibrary)` with no `allowUnsafe`, so any pointer fixture emits CS0227 — Acceptance 18 forbids a new expected-compiler-error exception and the contract forbids touching the runner. Pointer coverage is proven by the array fixture plus the shared `TypeTree` recursion, not by a pointer fixture. Stated, not silently dropped.
8. A guarded type that is only an inferred intermediate, never written and never carried by a declared symbol — `Factory.MakeList().Count` with no local. W sees the receiver type and the member; C sees nothing. Covered by the member half, which is the reach that matters.

Direct scanner tests, `WrittenNameScannerTests.cs` — a probe analyzer declared in the test project registers the scanner and reports every resolved symbol, so the LENS is tested apart from any rule's policy. Consuming-rule tests. AG0041 (`EngineInternalsOneDoorAnalyzerTests.cs`) gets Acceptance 8-11 with EXACT counts from the table, never `Assert.Single`, each diagnostic matched on id + span + message. Its reference fixture is the shared fake Engine source in `SharedAnalyzerSources.cs` carrying both grants — the mechanism `AnalyzerRunnerTests.cs:160-178` already proves works unchanged. Architecture tests — `LensOwnershipTests.cs`, built on a pure inspector so every check has both fixtures. `RepositoryFiles.FindRepositoryRoot()` (`RepositoryFiles.cs:25`) locates the tree; every `analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/*.cs` is read and parsed with `CSharpSyntaxTree.ParseText`; a `CSharpCompilation` is built whose references are the Roslyn assemblies already loaded in the test process, and symbols resolve against it. A resolution failure must fail the test, never yield an empty finding list.

The six checks, each separating duplicated scanning from unrelated analysis by RESOLVED SYMBOL, never by a name or a string:
- A1 written-name lens has one owner — every invocation whose target method is `RegisterSyntaxNodeAction` AND whose kind arguments include `SyntaxKind.IdentifierName` or `GenericName` (read with `GetConstantValue`, so AG0007's `CastExpression`/`AsExpression`/`DeclarationPattern`/`TypePattern` registrations separate out with no name test) must sit in `WrittenNameScanner`. NEGATIVE: a planted analyzer registering `IdentifierName`.
- A2 carried-type lens has one owner — `RegisterOperationAction(..., OperationKind.VariableDeclarator)` appears exactly once, in `DeclaredTypeScanner`; every `RegisterSymbolAction` whose handler reaches `TypeTree.Any` sits there too. NEGATIVE: a planted second `VariableDeclarator` registration.
- A3 consumers route through the owners — for AG0041, AG0023, AG0029 the `Initialize` body contains invocations whose target methods are declared on `WrittenNameScanner`, `DeclaredTypeScanner` and `MemberUseScanner` as its coverage requires, and contains NO direct `Register*` invocation on a Roslyn context type. NEGATIVE: a planted copy of AG0041 registering directly.
- A4 the caller-location check is `CompositionPoint`'s — each of AG0040, AG0023, AG0029 contains an invocation whose target method is DECLARED ON `CompositionPoint`. NEGATIVE: a planted rule whose caller test is `containingSymbol.Name == "Create"`.

## 1. THE MEASUREMENTS THAT DECIDE THE DESIGN

All run through the real driver (`CompilationWithAnalyzers.GetAnalyzerDiagnosticsAsync`) on Roslyn 4.14.0, the pinned version, in a throwaway project outside the repository.

**(a) The analyzer driver DOES visit documentation-comment crefs, and they resolve.** A `<see cref="Guarded"/>` on a method produces `NODE 'Guarded' kind=IdentifierName parent=NameMemberCref sym=NamedType:G.Guarded inTrivia=True`. A dotted cref `<see cref="Guarded.Member"/>` produces TWO nodes — the type (`parent=QualifiedCref`) and the member (`parent=NameMemberCref`) — both resolved. This falsifies enforcement-first's assertion that crefs are not visited, and confirms coverage-complete's measurement.

**(b) `ContainingSymbol` cannot satisfy Acceptance 12.** For the same call written directly in `Create()`, inside a lambda in `Create()`, and inside a local function in `Create()`, `OperationAnalysisContext.ContainingSymbol` and `SyntaxNodeAnalysisContext.ContainingSymbol` BOTH return `Method:Create/Ordinary` in all three cases. `SemanticModel.GetEnclosingSymbol(position)` returns `Method:Create/Ordinary`, `Method:lambda expression/AnonymousFunction`, and `Method:Nested()/LocalFunction` respectively. A caller check built on `ContainingSymbol` permits exactly what Acceptance 12 requires reported.

**(c) A `.Parent` walk from a cref node never reaches the method declaration.** Measured chain: `IdentifierName>NameMemberCref>XmlCrefAttribute>XmlEmptyElement>XmlElement>SingleLineDocumentationCommentTrivia`. Structured trivia terminates the chain. So enforcement-first's `IsInOwnBody` conjunction ALSO reports the doc comment on `Create()` — by a different route, to the same place. Both proposed caller designs report it.

**(d) The member-use lens fails OPEN where the written-name lens does not.** With `OperationKind.Invocation` and `ObjectCreation` registered: `[Guarded]` with a required constructor argument omitted (CS7036) produces NO `ObjectCreation` operation at all, while `[Guarded(1)]` produces one. `Guarded.Member(1, 2)` (CS1501) and `Guarded.NoSuch()` (CS0117) produce NO `Invocation` operation. In every one of those cases the written-name lens still resolves the guarded TYPE — `GetSymbolInfo` returns null with `CandidateReason=OverloadResolutionFailure` and `GetTypeInfo` returns `NamedType:GuardedAttribute`. This is the fail-closed payoff and the justification for the second tier.

**(e) A generic type written with arguments is ONE `GenericName` node.** `(Cache<int>)obj` in a cast resolves through the `GenericName` node alone; its identifier is a token, not a child `IdentifierName`. Drop `SyntaxKind.GenericName` and there is no other node to catch it.

**(f) `RegisterSymbolAction(SymbolKind.Method)` never fires for a local function**, and there is no `SymbolKind.Event` registration. A local-function parameter, a lambda parameter, and an `event EventHandler<Guarded>` are invisible to the carried-type lens and covered only by the written-name lens.

**(g) A local declared inside a lambda in `Create()` has `ILocalSymbol.ContainingSymbol = Method:lambda expression/AnonymousFunction`**, while the operation context's `ContainingSymbol` is `Method:Create`. The two disagree; only the enclosing-symbol answer is right.

**(h) A `DiagnosticAnalyzer` cannot be declared in `AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests`.** Reproduced: RS1038, RS1041, RS1036, RS2008, RS1025, RS1026, all errors under `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`.

**(i) Registration inventory, live.** `SyntaxKind.IdentifierName`/`GenericName`: **0** registrations. `OperationKind.VariableDeclarator`: **1** (`ContractConcreteTypeMustNotBeReferencedAnalyzer.cs:52`). The conjunction {Field, Property, Method} per declaring type: **1**. `ContainingSymbol` reads: **7**, all 7 already flowing into `CompositionPoint` or `OwnerClass.EnclosingType`. `GetEnclosingSymbol`: **0**. `TypeTree.Any` callers: **2**, both unrelated (`ContractPattern.cs:50`, `ReturnTypesMustNotBeTuplesAnalyzer.cs:131`).

A DiagnosticAnalyzer cannot be declared in AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests, so any design driving a scanner through a test-project probe analyzer is unbuildable. Anyone reasoning about the carried-type lens as 'all declared types' will believe those positions are double-covered when they are single-covered, and will delete the written-name registration as redundant.

A leaf test written as ContainingAssembly.Name == "AgentGuard.Engine" without a symbol-kind switch fires on namespace nodes: measured, a namespace symbol carries a non-null ContainingAssembly, and locals, parameters and type parameters carry the compilation's own. The first false positive appears on the using directive of every consumer, and the reflex fix is to special-case namespaces rather than to switch on kind. Every consumer's leaf test must switch on symbol kind FIRST: ITypeSymbol through TypeTree.Any, member symbols judged by ContainingType, everything else ignored.

analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/AttributeIdentity.cs is NOT in the contract's Surfaces and the extraction edits one method in it. If Tim says no, build RecoverBoundType in WrittenNameScanner and file the collapse as a GitHub issue rather than leaving it unrecorded.

The compiled analyzer-source model is useless without a synthesized global-usings tree: measured 156 compiler errors without it (CS0246 ×66 on Func<,>, CS0103 ×62 on StringComparison, CS1503 ×26, CS1955 ×2), because Directory.Build.props:15 sets ImplicitUsings=enable and the analyzer sources rely on it. With one 7-line global-using tree the compilation is clean over 82 files. AnalyzerSourceModel must assert zero errors BEFORE any query runs. Its reference set is 'whatever Roslyn the test host loaded'; if that ever skews from the pinned 4.14.0 the zero-error assertion turns it into a red test rather than a silent wrong answer, but it will be a red test nobody expected, so its failure message must name the assembly set and the first errors.

AG0041 uses CompositionPoint's method IDENTITY, not its caller-location check. The revision brief says 'each of the four consuming analyzers actually uses CompositionPoint's caller-location check'; the contract gives AG0041 a callee restriction with no caller constraint ('Every public Engine API stays reachable'), and AG0017 already pins who may call SystemServices.Create(). The enforcement matrix therefore requires IsInsideContainerFactory from the three one-door rules and IsContainerFactory from AG0041. SystemServices.cs:91 declares the local as IPlatformServices (an Abstractions type), so PlatformServices never appears as a carried type in Create(), while AG0023's CrossPlatformAdapters adapters = CrossPlatformAdapters.Create(); at line 90 is real. Acceptance 21 still requires AG0029 to prove the accept path 'including as the declared type of a local', so it must be a SYNTHETIC fixture. AG0041 and AG0023/AG0029 fixtures written with public members over internal types do not compile: CS0050 and CS0051 for a public member carrying an internal type, CS0060 for a public class deriving from an internal base. AnalyzerRunner throws unless every such error is declared, and Acceptance 18 forbids introducing a new expected-compiler-error exception. Every consumer fixture member must be internal. The same fixture with internal members compiles cleanly and the lenses still report.

The written-name and carried-type lenses deliberately overlap: every ordinary declaration trips both, and a var local trips the written-name lens with the inferred type (measured: var is an IdentifierName resolving to the inferred type). The contract blesses it ('a fact the tests must accommodate rather than a requirement they must prove'), but every new fixture author must be told, or the first double report will be filed as a defect.

The one allowed exception must carry the issue number in whatever check names it, or it decays into a permanent exemption the next reader takes as sanctioned duplication.

Six new file names need Tim's yes before RULE-PHASE builds against them: WrittenNameScanner.cs (the one the contract explicitly reserved) plus AnalyzerSourceModel.cs, SharedLensOwnershipTests.cs, BoundaryRuleWiringTests.cs, WrittenNameScannerTests.cs and DeclaredTypeScannerTests.cs. autoResolved.choice: Whether the method-level caller check reads context.ContainingSymbol, walks syntax ancestors, or calls SemanticModel.GetEnclosingSymbol.
autoResolved.resolution: CompositionPoint.IsInsideContainerFactory(SemanticModel, position, CancellationToken) calls GetEnclosingSymbol and tests the result with IsContainerFactory. No syntax ancestor walk, and no ContainingSymbol read at any consumer.
autoResolved.principle: rails-dry-code rail 8 — 'When work needs a capability a BCL, OS, or OSS primitive already provides, default to reusing that primitive… A tested BCL/OS/OSS primitive was reimplemented from scratch or hand-composed from lower-level calls to avoid giving it an owner' is the Violation; the one-owner rule is the forcing function to pick CompositionPoint, not a bar to reuse. Reinforced by best-practices guide 6a, 'Never scaffold or wire a check to pass.'
autoResolved.evidence: Judge's probe on Roslyn 4.14.0 through CompilationWithAnalyzers, five positions: direct in Create() → GetEnclosingSymbol Method:Sub.Host.Create()/Ordinary (permit); inside a lambda in Create() → Method:lambda expression/AnonymousFunction (report, Acceptance 12); inside a local function in Create() → Method:Nested()/LocalFunction (report, Acceptance 12); another method → that method (report); a cref in Create()'s doc comment → NamedType:Sub.Host (report). context.ContainingSymbol returns Method:Create for the first FOUR of those, so it permits the Acceptance-12 bypass. The syntax-walk alternative hand-composes what GetEnclosingSymbol already computes, and is additionally wrong-by-accident on the trivia case: the .Parent chain from a cref terminates at SingleLineDocumentationCommentTrivia and never reaches MethodDeclaration. GetEnclosingSymbol has zero uses in the analyzer project today, so giving it one deliberate owner costs nothing.

autoResolved.choice: Whether WrittenNameScanner writes its own name resolution or the two-tier mechanic AttributeIdentity already owns is extracted into one owner.
autoResolved.resolution: Extract: WrittenNameScanner.RecoverBoundType holds the GetTypeInfo tier, and AttributeIdentity.ResolveAttributeType calls it while keeping its own tier 1 (constructor → containing type) and its syntactic …Attribute fallback. AG0008 and AG0105 behaviour is unchanged.
autoResolved.principle: rails-dry-code rail 4 ('a capability ruled "reuse" calls the existing owner; one ruled "extract" collapses the copies into a single shared owner and calls it') together with rail 6 ('a duplicated block or whole function — same logic even with renamed variables').
autoResolved.evidence: AttributeIdentity.cs:60-72 is the live two-tier body, with a four-line comment stating exactly why the second tier exists. The judge measured the same recovery is required at the NAME-NODE level: for [Guarded] with the required constructor argument omitted, GetSymbolInfo returns Symbol=null with CandidateReason=OverloadResolutionFailure and CandidateSymbols=[the constructor], while GetTypeInfo returns NamedType:G.GuardedAttribute — and MemberUseScanner produces NO ObjectCreation operation for that attribute, versus one for the well-formed [Guarded(1)]. A second implementation of the tier would be a literal copy of AttributeIdentity.cs:69-71. Tier 1 is NOT shared: AttributeIdentity narrows a constructor to its type, while WrittenNameScanner must keep the symbol because AG0041 governs internal Engine MEMBERS as well as types.

autoResolved.choice: Whether the general written-name lens inherits AG0008's syntactic simple-name fallback for a name that binds to nothing in either tier.
autoResolved.resolution: No. Resolve returns (null, null) and the consumer is not invoked. The fallback stays inside AttributeIdentity with AG0008 and AG0105. Unresolvable fixtures are instead required to declare their compiler errors.
autoResolved.principle: Best-practices guide 3a, 'Take the least privilege and the narrowest scope that works', read with 5a (fail closed is the default — the unresolved case is never silently JUDGED, which is different from guessing at it).
autoResolved.evidence: The guarded-type set is an assembly-plus-namespace identity (WellKnownType.IsInAssembly, WellKnownType.cs:66); a bare simple-name match can assert neither half, so a name fallback would widen the rule from an identity match to a name match — reporting unrelated same-named types, not failing closed. The fallback is fail-closed only where the candidate set is a fixed known list of BCL attributes, which is AG0008's case and not this one. The loud failure path already exists: AnalyzerRunner.ThrowOnUnexpectedCompilerErrors (AnalyzerRunner.cs:193) throws on any undeclared compiler error, and an unresolved identifier in an Engine/CLI/TestHelpers compilation already fails the build with CS0246.

autoResolved.choice: How the direct scanner tests exercise internal scanners whose registration context is a sealed, non-constructible CompilationStartAnalysisContext — declare a probe DiagnosticAnalyzer in the test project and suppress the RS rules it trips, or factor the judgment into pure functions.
autoResolved.resolution: Factor the judgment out: WrittenNameScanner.Resolve and DeclaredTypeScanner.CarriedTypes are pure and internal, the registrations are thin wrappers over them, and the tests drive the pure functions through AnalyzerRunner.CompileAsync. No RS rule is suppressed and no globalconfig is edited.
autoResolved.principle: rails-decisions, 'Exception to a settled rule' — reaching for a suppression because doing it right is more work is the Violation; and best-practices guide 6a, 'Never weaken, skip, or delete a test to get a green build; fix the code instead.'
autoResolved.evidence: Reproduced by the judge: a project mirroring AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests.csproj (net10.0, Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Workspaces, TreatWarningsAsErrors=true from Directory.Build.props:36) fails to build a DiagnosticAnalyzer with six errors — RS1038, RS1041, RS1036, RS2008, RS1025, RS1026. eng/agentguard-test-analyzer-relaxations.globalconfig carries only SA0001, SA1600, CS1591, CA1707, CA1515 and CA2007, so making the probe build would mean adding six more. The correct path already has an explicit invitation and a live precedent: AnalyzerRunner.CompileAsync's own doc comment says it exists 'so a test can drive an internal helper (for example BoundaryServices.Resolve) directly rather than only through an analyzer's diagnostics', DerivedBoundaryServicesTests.cs does exactly that, and AgentGuard.Analyzers.csproj already grants InternalsVisibleTo("AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests").

autoResolved.choice: Whether ownership checks may be text scans over analyzer source files, the idiom the two existing structural tests use.
autoResolved.resolution: No. Every ownership and wiring check binds registration arguments, kind constants, gate constants and call targets to SYMBOLS over a compiled model of the analyzer project. Only the repository-root walk and the bin/obj exclusion are reused from the text idiom.
autoResolved.principle: rails-real-work rail 2 ('a check hard-wired, special-cased, or gamed to pass is worse than no check — the metric must measure reality') with rails-solid-code rail 3 ('encode the general rule; match on the structural property, not the concrete instance').
autoResolved.evidence: The first round's caller check was 'the literal "Create" must not appear in these four files' — green on any hand-rolled walk that never spells the literal (method.Name.Length == 6, a nameof, a shared constant) and red on a comment. Its carried-type companion ('only DeclaredTypeScanner.cs may call TypeTree.Any') is false on the live tree today: the judge measured exactly two callers, ContractPattern.cs:50 and ReturnTypesMustNotBeTuplesAnalyzer.cs:131, and the contract's own reuse ledger directs three more. The symbol-resolved form separates the live populations correctly with no edits: five analyzer types reach CompositionPoint transitively while the two one-door analyzers reach none, and exactly one declaring type registers Field+Property+Method together.

autoResolved.resolution: The CONJUNCTION SymbolKind.Field AND Property AND Method per declaring type, plus OperationKind.VariableDeclarator as a second independent assertion. Not the kinds individually, and not VariableDeclarator alone.
